title: Hereditary discrepancy and factorization norms (AimPL) — Problem 1.15: Beck-Fiala conjecture and making it constructive

problems.sourceStatement: Given a set system $(V,\mathcal{S})$ with $V=[n]$, $\mathcal{S}=S_1,...,S_m$. Each $i\in V$ occurs in at most $t$ sets from $\mathcal{S}$. Then there is a coloring to the elements of $V$ achieving a discrepancy of $O(\sqrt{t})$. Komlós conjecture implies this by treating the incidence vector of each $i\in V$ as a vector and scaling it down by $\sqrt{t}$.
problems.problem: Prove the Beck-Fiala conjecture: every set system in which each element belongs to at most $t$ sets has a 2-coloring of discrepancy $O(\sqrt{t})$, with the bound independent of the number of elements and sets. A constructive (polynomial-time) version is also sought.
problems.wordDescription: The Beck-Fiala conjecture is the most famous open problem for sparse set systems: it asserts that maximum degree $t$ forces discrepancy $O(\sqrt{t})$, far better than the linear $2t-1$ bound of the Beck-Fiala theorem. The Komlós conjecture implies it by scaling incidence vectors by $1/\sqrt{t}$. Progress on the pure bound has been slow ($2t-3$, then $2t - \log^* t$ by Bukh), while Banaszczyk's vector-balancing theorem gives the much better $O(\sqrt{t\log n})$ at the price of dependence on $n$ and a non-constructive proof. The algorithmic question was largely resolved: Bansal (2010), Lovett-Meka (2012) and Rothvoss (2014) achieved $O(\sqrt{t}\log n)$ constructively, and Bansal-Dadush-Garg (2016) made Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{t\log n})$ bound constructive. In 2025 Bansal and Jiang resolved the conjecture itself for all degrees $t \geq \log^2 n$ and gave $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{\log n})$ for $t \leq \log^2 n$, so the full conjecture is now known up to $\mathrm{poly}(\log\log n)$ factors, with only the small-degree regime $t < \log^2 n$ remaining.
problems.mathematicalConditions: For a set system $(V, \mathcal{S})$ with $|V| = n$, $|\mathcal{S}| = m$, such that every $i \in V$ lies in at most $t$ of the sets $S_1, \dots, S_m$, there exists a coloring $\chi: V \to \{-1, 1\}$ with $\max_{j \in [m]} \left|\sum_{i \in S_j} \chi(i)\right| = O(\sqrt{t})$, where the constant is absolute (independent of $n, m, t$). The constructive version asks for a polynomial-time algorithm finding such a coloring.

literature.title: J. Beck, T. Fiala, 'Integer-making' theorems, Discrete Applied Mathematics 3(1):1-8, 1981
literature.description: Proves the Beck-Fiala theorem: discrepancy at most $2t-1$ for systems of maximum degree $t$, and states the conjecture that $O(\sqrt{t})$ is the truth.

literature.title: D. Bednarchak, M. Helm, A note on the Beck-Fiala theorem, Combinatorica 17(1):147-149, 1997; M. Helm, On the Beck-Fiala theorem, Discrete Mathematics 207:207, 1999
literature.description: Small improvements of the Beck-Fiala bound to $2t-3$ (for $t \geq 3$).

literature.title: B. Bukh, An improvement of the Beck-Fiala theorem, Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 25(3):380-398, 2016
literature.description: Improves the Beck-Fiala bound to $2t - \log^* t$, where $\log^*$ is the iterated logarithm — the best bound depending only on $t$.

literature.title: W. Banaszczyk, Balancing vectors and Gaussian measures of n-dimensional convex bodies, Random Structures & Algorithms 12(4):351-360, 1998
literature.description: Implies the $O(\sqrt{t\log n})$ (equivalently $O(\sqrt{t\log m})$) bound for degree-$t$ systems, non-constructively.

literature.title: N. Bansal, S. Garg, Algorithmic discrepancy beyond partial coloring, STOC 2017 (arXiv:1611.01805; first posted as arXiv:1512.02074)
literature.description: A framework going beyond the partial-coloring method; the AimPL page credits it with the $O(\sqrt{t\log n\log|S_j|})$ guarantee in the $t$-sparse setting and it improved algorithmic bounds for Tusnády's and Steinitz problems.

literature.title: N. Bansal, H. Jiang, Decoupling via affine spectral-independence: Beck-Fiala and Komlós bounds beyond Banaszczyk, arXiv:2508.3961, 2025
literature.description: Resolves the Beck-Fiala conjecture for $t \geq \log^2 n$ and gives $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{\log n})$ for $t \leq \log^2 n$, improving on Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{t\log n})$; all bounds are algorithmic.

problems.verificationNotes: Verified on 2026-08-25. The statements on the page are consistent with the literature: Beck-Fiala (1981) gives $2t-1$; Bukh's $2t - \log^* t$ is published in Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 25 (2016) 380-398 (also stated in Theory of Computing 15(15), 2019); Banaszczyk's non-constructive bound is quoted as $O(\sqrt{t\log\min\{n,m\}})$ in the literature. '[Bansal-Garg'15]' refers to Bansal-Garg, 'Algorithmic discrepancy beyond partial coloring', first posted December 2015 and published at STOC 2017 (arXiv:1611.01805). Bansal-Jiang (arXiv:2508.3961, 2025) confirmed: resolves the conjecture for $t \geq \log^2 n$ and gives $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{t}+\sqrt{\log n})$ for $t \leq \log^2 n$.
problems.statusDetails: A $2t-1$ guarantee which is also algorithmic was given by Beck-Fiala. Recently, [Bukh] gave a guarantee of $2t-\log^*t$. Banaszczyk's result implies a bound of $O(\sqrt{t\log m})$ but is non-constructive. Other algorithmic guarantees are $O(\sqrt{t}\log n)$ [Bansal'10, Lovett-Meka'12, Rothvoss'15] and $O(\sqrt{t\log n\log|S_j|})$ [Bansal-Garg'15]. Bansal and Jiang (2025) resolved the conjecture for $t \geq \log^2 n$ and gave $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{\log n})$ for $t \leq \log^2 n$; the conjecture is open only in the regime $t < \log^2 n$.
